todos.description: Pass the Tags dialog location to Lightroom and record the metadata survey
todos.context: The app already writes xmp:Rating in place inside the JPEG's embedded XMP packet and the stock tags dc:title/dc:description/dc:subject into that packet, into the EXIF as a fallback, and into the .xmp sidecar beside a RAW pair. The survey behind this todo found one real loss: the Location field of the Tags dialog is pasted into the claude prompt and then thrown away, although everything here goes to microstock through Lightroom and an editorial submission is required to carry the place. Colour labels were considered and deliberately rejected - they stay in .photo-colors.json and nothing is written to xmp:Label.

plan.summary: Todo #9 started as a survey of what else the app could hand to Lightroom. The survey's answer, settled with the user: colour labels are deliberately NOT written - they stay in .photo-colors.json and xmp:Label is dropped from the todo - and the one real gap is the Location field of the Tags dialog (internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go:97), which the user fills, the prompt consumes as a Location: line, and nothing ever records in the file. Since everything here ends up on microstock through Lightroom and sometimes Photoshop, where an editorial submission must carry its place, the branch writes that place: Iptc4xmpCore:Location always, plus photoshop:City/State/Country whenever the model manages to split the free text, into the same two carriers the tags already use - the JPEG's XMP packet in place and the .xmp sidecar beside the RAW pair. There is no EXIF tag for a place, so the EXIF fallback path carries the tags but not the place and says so. The work is mostly in internal/core/imaging: the property machinery in sidecar.go and xmp_packet.go is dc-shaped throughout (descriptionOpen hardcodes xmlns:dc, openDescription binds only that with errForeignDC as the escape hatch, stripProperties removes only the three dc properties, sidecarProperties emits only them) and becomes a table of owned properties across three namespaces. The prompt and the CLI json-schema gain the optional split, and README records the survey - what is written, what this branch adds, what is rejected and why, plus the two pipeline traps that silently undo the work: Lightroom reads embedded XMP at import only, and Minimize Embedded Metadata / Save for Web strip it.

steps.title: Record the survey
steps.details: A new section in README.md under Features listing, per field, what is written and where: xmp:Rating; dc:title + dc:description + dc:subject; Iptc4xmpCore:Location; photoshop:City/State/Country - with the packet -> EXIF fallback -> RAW sidecar rule and the note that a place has no EXIF carrier. README answers 'what ends up in my file' and nothing else: the rejected half of the survey is development rationale and goes into the comment above the owned-properties table two steps later, where a reader would ask why a property is missing from it, and Lightroom's and Photoshop's own ways of losing metadata are not this app's behaviour and are not documented at all. No Go changes in this step.

steps.title: Give the tags a place
steps.details: In internal/core/model/tags.go add type Place struct {Location, City, State, Country string} and a Place field on model.Tags. Equal compares it; IsEmpty keeps looking at the title and the keywords only - it guards 'claude returned no tags' in tagger.go, the sidecar-overwrite rule in stock_info.go and the foreign-dc refusal in xmp_packet.go:appendDescription, and a place alone must not count as a result in any of them. Add Place.IsEmpty() and a Trimmed() for the writers. Table-driven tests in internal/core/model/tags_test.go.

steps.title: Read the place out of an XMP document
steps.details: parseSidecar in internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go keeps dcNamespace elements and, through isRatingName, xmp:Rating. Generalise that into a table of the properties the app owns - namespace + local name -> setter - and add Iptc4xmpCore:Location (namespace http://iptc.org/std/Iptc4xmpCore/1.0/xmlns/) and photoshop:City/State/Country (namespace http://ns.adobe.com/photoshop/1.0/). Cover both the element form and the attribute form in readAttributes, the shape exiftool and simple writers use, and fill Place in sidecarTags.tags(). Read only - nothing writes yet. Tests in sidecar_test.go: element form, attribute form, a Lightroom sidecar carrying both a place and crs:*, a document with no place, and a prefix bound to a foreign namespace being ignored.

steps.title: Write the place into the RAW sidecar
steps.details: The writer half of sidecar.go is dc-shaped: descriptionOpen hardcodes xmlns:dc, openDescription binds only that with errForeignDC as the escape hatch, stripProperties removes only the three dc properties and sidecarProperties emits only them. Turn that into a table of owned properties {prefix, namespace, name, value} and drive all four from it. The comment above that table carries the rejected half of the survey so nobody redoes it: xmp:Label (colour labels stay in .photo-colors.json by the user's decision), lr:hierarchicalSubject (Lightroom-only, agencies ignore it, our keywords are flat), xmp:CreateDate and photoshop:DateCreated (would move the photo's date, which the app preserves), GPS, photoshop:Headline/Instructions, Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo and plus:ModelReleaseStatus (no field in the app produces them), and crs:* (Lightroom's own, preserved byte for byte). stripProperties gains one pattern per new property in element, self-closing and attribute form - one pattern per property, never an alternation, for the reason the comment on dcElementPatterns gives. openDescription binds every namespace actually being written, and the errForeignDC escape hatch becomes per-prefix, falling back to insertDescription for the ones that clash. sidecarProperties writes Iptc4xmpCore:Location and the photoshop:* fields as plain text elements, not rdf:Alt, skipping the empty ones. WriteSidecar keeps its signature - the place travels inside model.Tags - so tags_action.go and tags_runs.go are untouched. Tests: a new sidecar; a Lightroom sidecar where every crs:* property survives byte for byte; a place replaced; a place cleared; a document binding photoshop to a foreign vocabulary; a round trip through parseSidecar.

steps.title: Write the place into the JPEG packet
steps.details: appendDescription in internal/core/imaging/xmp_packet.go builds one rdf:Description declaring xmlns:dc and fills it from sidecarProperties, and emptyDescriptionPattern drops that description once it is empty. Both follow the table from the previous step, so the appended description declares every namespace it uses and is still recognised as empty when nothing is written into it. The length rule of rewritePacket is unchanged: what does not fit in the padding is not written here at all. The EXIF fallback in exif_write.go has no carrier for a place, so WriteStockTags must report when it falls back with a non-empty place - the tags reach the EXIF, the place does not - in the same message that already tells the user the file was rewritten. Tests in xmp_packet_test.go and exif_write_test.go: place written into a packet with room; a packet too small (refused, tags fall back, place reported as not written); place cleared; a packet already carrying a rating keeping it.

steps.title: Ask the model for the split
steps.details: In internal/core/tags/tagger.go extend tagsSchema with optional city, state and country strings - required stays [title, keywords] and additionalProperties stays false, so an answer without them is still valid. Extend claudeResponse.StructuredOutput and fill model.Tags.Place from it; Request carries the free-text location so Place.Location is set from what the user typed, not from what the model echoed. In internal/core/tags/prompts/stock_photo.txt add the three fields to the response format section and say in the location section that when the Location: line is present the place is also split into city, region and country and returned in those fields, in ASCII, leaving a level empty rather than guessing it, and that without a Location: line all three stay empty in commercial mode. Tests in tagger_test.go: a response with the split, one without it, one with a partial split, and that the free-text location survives either way.

steps.title: Carry the place through the dialog
steps.details: TagsDialog.Tags() in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go rebuilds model.Tags from the two result entries and would drop the place. Keep the split in a field set by showTags and SetPhotoInfo, and have Tags() take Location from the live d.location entry and the three levels from that field, dropping the split when the entry no longer matches the text it was derived from, so an edited location cannot ship a stale city. The split stays invisible in the dialog; the free-text field is the only thing the user edits. Tests in tags_dialog_test.go: a generated split reaches Tags(); editing the location entry afterwards clears it; SetPhotoInfo from a file with a place fills the location entry only while it is untouched.

questions.question: Should this todo stop after the survey and leave the file writing to a separate todo?
questions.answer: No. The survey plus the location, in one branch. xmp:Label is dropped entirely: colour labels are never written to files.

questions.question: A photo can carry Red+Green at once but xmp:Label is a single string. How is that resolved?
questions.answer: Moot: colour labels are not written to files at all.

questions.question: How does the free-text Location field reach the file?
questions.answer: The dialog keeps one free-text field, always written to Iptc4xmpCore:Location. The prompt additionally asks for a city/state/country split; when it comes back, those are written to photoshop:City/State/Country too.

questions.question: Which carriers does the place go into?
questions.answer: The JPEG XMP packet and the RAW sidecar, exactly like the tags.

questions.question: The Editorial checkbox and its date also live only in the prompt. Are they in scope?
questions.answer: No - the prompt already builds the 'City, Country - Month D, YYYY' caption prefix into the title, so there is nothing to do.

questions.question: Is a place found in a file read back into the app?
questions.answer: Yes, unlike colours: the place round-trips through the sidecar and the packet the way the tags do, so reopening the dialog shows what the file holds.

questions.question: Should the place fall back to the EXIF when the JPEG has no writable XMP packet?
questions.answer: No. There is no EXIF tag for a place, so such a JPEG keeps its place only in the RAW sidecar and the write reports that the place was not written.

risks: The last two imaging steps rewrite the machinery that already writes the tags: the errForeignDC path, the empty-description removal and the length rule of rewritePacket all change shape. The 621 lines of sidecar_test.go and 643 of xmp_packet_test.go are the safety net and must all keep passing unchanged in meaning.

stripProperties is shared by the sidecar writer and the packet writer, so a new pattern that is too greedy eats the crs:* develop settings of a Lightroom sidecar - the exact damage the one-pattern-per-property rule exists to prevent.
IsEmpty must keep ignoring the place: three call sites read it as 'this is not a result', and a place-only Tags slipping through would clear a sidecar or blank the dialog.
The split is invisible in the dialog, so a wrong city cannot be corrected by hand, only by editing the location and generating again.
The place has no EXIF carrier, so on the fallback path it is absent unless the write reports it.
The json-schema change must not make a well-formed old answer fail: the three new fields stay optional.

Out of scope but named by the survey: creator/copyright (dc:creator, dc:rights, xmpRights:UsageTerms) and release status (plus:ModelReleaseStatus) are the next microstock candidates and each deserves its own todo.

todos.description: Improve keyboard navigation in the Tags dialog
todos.context: In the Tags dialog (internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go) the button row is rebuilt by setGenerating(bool): while a run is in flight it shows Cancel (N) | Background (B) | disabled Generate, idle it shows Close (ESC) | Copy title | Copy keywords | [Save JPEG] | Generate; N and B are not handled by the dialog but by global GLFW scancode shortcuts on the canvas (internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, mapped to OnCancel/OnBlue and dispatched through internal/gui/app/actions.go + tags_action.go, gated by shortcutsBlocked), so they only fire when nothing holds focus and Generating() calls window.Canvas().Unfocus() as a workaround. Escape is already solved separately by the escapeEntry/escapeDateEntry/escapeCheck wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go, which intercept Escape in TypedKey and forward it to TagsDialogCallbacks.OnEscape because a Fyne calendar popup can stack over the dialog; the dialog otherwise relies on default Fyne Tab traversal across Concept, Location, Editorial, Date, claude path, Title, Keywords and the buttons, and this fragile letter-key/focus interaction is what prompted the task.

plan.summary: Move the Tags dialog's keyboard handling into the dialog itself so it no longer depends on canvas-level GLFW scancode shortcuts firing only while nothing holds focus (and on the `window.Canvas().Unfocus()` workaround in `Generating()`). The escape wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go become a general key router that every focusable widget of the dialog (entries, date entry, check, and a new button wrapper) consults before the embedded widget sees the key; multi-line entries stop swallowing Tab, so Tab traversal actually walks the whole dialog; buttons answer Return as well as Space and, while a run is going, N/B by physical key; and focus is placed deliberately (Concept on open, Cancel while a run goes, a sensible field when the run ends) instead of being cleared. Help text and CLAUDE.md are updated last. The app-side plumbing (actions.go, tags_action.go, shortcuts.go) keeps working unchanged as a fallback for when nothing in the dialog holds focus.

steps.title: Turn the escape wrappers into a key router and let Tab leave the multi-line fields
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/escapable.go replace the `onEscape func()` field of `escapeEntry`, `escapeDateEntry` and `escapeCheck` with `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` calls it first and returns when it reports the key as consumed, otherwise it forwards to the embedded widget. Rename the three types to `dialogEntry`, `dialogDateEntry`, `dialogCheck` (file name stays escapable.go) and rewrite the file header comment: it is no longer only about Escape. Add `func (e *dialogEntry) AcceptsTab() bool { return false }` — the GLFW driver checks `fyne.Tabbable.AcceptsTab()` in `capturesTab` *before* `TypedKey`, so a multi-line `widget.Entry` (Title, Keywords) currently eats Tab and cannot be left by keyboard; overriding it is the only way to make Tab traverse. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` that consumes `fyne.KeyEscape` by calling `d.requestEscape()` and returns false otherwise, and pass `d.handleKey` to every constructor in `buildInputs`/`buildResult`; update the struct field types. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go update the `[]*escapeEntry` loop in TestTagsDialog_Escape to `[]*dialogEntry` and add cases: Tab is not accepted by title/keywords (`assert.False(t, d.keywords.AcceptsTab())`) and a non-Escape key still reaches the widget (the existing "other keys still reach the input" case covers the latter).

steps.title: Give the dialog buttons keyboard activation and the run's command keys
steps.details: Add a `dialogButton` wrapper to internal/gui/ui/escapable.go embedding `widget.Button` with an `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` asks the dialog first, then treats `fyne.KeyReturn`/`fyne.KeyEnter` as a tap (Fyne's Button only answers Space), then falls through to `widget.Button.TypedKey`. Add a helper to internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, e.g. `func physicalKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent, key glfw.Key, name fyne.KeyName) bool`, matching `ev.Physical.ScanCode == glfw.GetKeyScancode(key)` or `ev.Name == name` — the scancode form keeps the letters layout-independent like the canvas shortcuts, the name form is the fallback where GLFW is not initialised (it returns -1 then, which would make N and B collide). In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go build every button (`generateBtn`, `copyTitleBtn`, `copyKeywordsBtn`, `saveJPEGBtn`, `closeBtn`, `cancelRunBtn`, `backgroundBtn`) as `*dialogButton`, change `setEnabled(button *widget.Button, ...)` to take `*dialogButton`, and add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleCommandKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` = `handleKey` plus, while `d.generating`, N -> `call(d.callbacks.OnCancelRun)` and B -> `call(d.callbacks.OnBackground)`; hand `handleCommandKey` to the buttons and to `dialogCheck` (neither consumes runes, so intercepting bare letters there is safe, unlike in a text entry where the character still arrives through TypedRune). Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: N and B on the focused `cancelRunBtn` reach OnCancelRun/OnBackground only while generating; Return on a focused button taps it; N typed into `d.concept` triggers no callback.

steps.title: Place focus deliberately instead of clearing it
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add a `shown bool` field set in `Show()` (cleared in `Hide()`) and a small `func (d *TagsDialog) focus(obj fyne.Focusable)` that no-ops unless the dialog is shown — `canvas.Focus` logs "Failed to focus object which is not part of the canvas' content, menu or overlays" for an object in an unshown dialog. `Show()` focuses `d.concept` so the dialog opens ready for typing. `Generating()` drops `d.window.Canvas().Unfocus()` and instead focuses `d.cancelRunBtn` after `setGenerating(true)`, so N/B/Space/Return all act on the run without the unfocus trick; update the comment above it, which explains the workaround. `finishRun()` must move focus off the button that is about to leave the row (the focus manager keeps a pointer to a removed object and keys then go nowhere): focus `d.pathEntry` when `Fail` revealed `pathRow`, `d.title` when tags arrived, else `d.generateBtn`; the simplest shape is for `SetTags`/`Fail` to pass the target into `finishRun`. Tests: after `d.Show()` the canvas focus is the concept entry; after `Generating()` it is `cancelRunBtn`; after `SetTags`/`Fail` it is no longer a button that left `d.buttons.Objects`.

steps.title: Enter in the single-line inputs starts a run
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go extract the Generate button's body into `func (d *TagsDialog) startGenerate()` (guarding `d.generating` and `d.generateBtn.Disabled()`), use it for the button and set it as `OnSubmitted` of `d.concept`, `d.location` and `d.pathEntry` — Fyne fires `OnSubmitted` on Return for single-line entries, so a user can type a concept and press Enter without reaching for the mouse, while Return in the multi-line Title/Keywords keeps inserting a newline. Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: `d.concept.OnSubmitted("x")` (or a Return key event on the entry) runs OnGenerate once and puts the dialog into the generating state; a second submission while generating does nothing.

steps.title: Document the dialog's keys
steps.details: Extend the "Tags dialog" section of `helpRight` in internal/gui/ui/help.go with the keys the dialog now owns: `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` move between fields and buttons, `Space`/`Enter` press the focused button, `Enter` in Concept/Location starts a run, `Esc` closes, and keep `B`/`N` for background/cancel of a running generation. Mirror the same list in the "Keyboard Shortcuts" section of CLAUDE.md (the `B` and `N` bullets currently say "Tags dialog only" without saying that they now work from the dialog itself).

questions.question: Should the dialog focus the Concept field when it opens? It makes typing immediate but means the canvas letter shortcuts no longer reach the app while the dialog is up (they are blocked by shortcutsBlocked anyway). Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 3.
Should Tab move out of the multi-line Title/Keywords fields, giving up the ability to type a literal tab character there? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 1.
Should Enter in Concept/Location/claude-path start a generation? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 4.

Keep the global fallback (ui/shortcuts.go OnCancel/OnBlue -> app.handleCancel/handleBlue) now that the dialog answers N/B itself, or delete the tags branch of handleBlue? Assume keep — it still fires when a mouse click has left nothing focused. Affects step 2.

Keep the current button order (Close, Copy title, Copy keywords, Save JPEG, Generate), which is also the Tab order, or should Generate come first? Assume keep — the existing test asserts that exact slice. Affects steps 2 and 3.

risks: glfw.GetKeyScancode returns -1 when GLFW is not initialised (unit tests, headless CI), so a scancode-only match would make N and B indistinguishable; the helper must also compare fyne.KeyName.

Bare letters cannot be intercepted inside a text entry: the driver delivers TypedKey and TypedRune separately, so swallowing KeyN in TypedKey would still insert 'n'. Only the buttons and the check may claim letters.
The button row is rebuilt by setGenerating; if focus stays on a button that was removed from the container, the focus manager keeps pointing at it and keys silently go nowhere.
canvas.Focus on a widget whose dialog is not shown logs an error - the focus helper must be a no-op until Show().
Escape from the date entry while the Fyne calendar popup is stacked on top must keep going through OnEscape -> app.handleCancel, which is the only place that can see the foreign overlay.

Existing tests compare d.buttons.Objects by identity and call test.Tap on the buttons; changing the field type to *dialogButton keeps both working only if the wrapper embeds widget.Button and calls ExtendBaseWidget.

todos.description: Copy stock tags from one photo to another
todos.context: Let a user take the stock tags of one photo (model.Tags - Title + Keywords, plus a Place on the todo/9 branch) and apply them to another photo; today there is no UI affordance and no core entry point for it, only per-photo generation. The pieces to build on are the Tags dialog session in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, which owns the clipboard copies and the save path, the per-photo cache in internal/core/imaging/image_provider.go (PeekStockInfo/StoreStockInfo), and the writers ExifService.WriteStockTags (JPEG XMP packet with an EXIF fallback) and imaging.WriteSidecar (.xmp beside the RAW pair). Todo #9 is adding a Place to model.Tags and reshaping the sidecar and packet property tables, so whatever is copied has to carry the place too.

todos.description: Make sure tags edited by hand in the Tags dialog are written into the XMP
todos.context: Hand-edited Title and Keywords reach the RAW sidecar only when the dialog closes - tagsSession.close calls saveSidecar(s.dialog.Tags()) in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, guarded by photo.HasRAW and skipped when the tags equal s.saved - while the run-finished paths write the sidecar from the run result instead (runFinished and the detached tagRunner.finishDetached in internal/gui/app/tags_runs.go). The JPEG's embedded XMP packet is written only through the explicit Save JPEG button (OnSaveJPEG -> tagsSession.saveJPEG -> ExifService.WriteStockTags), a button that exists only for a JPEG and is enabled only while model.Tags.Problems() is empty, so hand edits to a JPEG that are merely closed never enter the packet. Values come from TagsDialog.Tags(), which reads the live entry text, and every successful write also refreshes the per-photo cache through StoreStockInfo.
